text: The Patriots put on a dominant display Sunday against Las Vegas, demolishing the Raiders 45-17 at Gillette Stadium despite operating without several key contributors—Drake Maye accounted for five total touchdowns in the rout, managing the feat without his top receiver and with both starting cornerbacks unavailable. The victory came at a cost, however, as the team suffered multiple injuries in the win: running back TreVeyon Henderson departed with an ankle injury, left tackle Will Campbell exited with what's believed to be a knee sprain, and the Patriots had already placed veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve Saturday with a calf injury. The fact that New England's offense and defense operated so effectively despite this collection of absences speaks to the depth and execution Coach Mike Vrabel has assembled, though the coming weeks will test just how deep that well runs with Henderson, Campbell, and Hollins sidelined.
